title: Equilibrium and Pricing in Consumer Networks with Nonlinear Utilities: An Online Shape-Constrained Learning Approach
summary: We study optimal monopoly pricing over consumer networks governed by general nonlinear utilities. In our framework, a consumer's utility is jointly determined by an individualized price and the consumption choices of their peers, propagated through a directed and signed social graph. This formulation encapsulates a broad class of utility functions; it strictly generalizes the traditional linear-quadratic framework to include logit-type discrete choice, isoelastic, and Stone-Geary utilities under a single theoretical umbrella.
